title: Stress Tests - Federal Reserve Board
summary: This Federal Reserve webpage describes the agency's stress testing program and capital planning framework for large banks, explaining how the stress capital buffer (SCB) integrates stress test results with regulatory capital requirements. The page outlines the evolution from the separate Dodd-Frank Act Stress Test and CCAR (2013-2019) to the unified SCB framework implemented in 2020. It notes that the largest supervised banking organizations have more than doubled their aggregate common equity capital since 2009.
key_points: The stress test is a forward-looking quantitative evaluation demonstrating how a hypothetical macroeconomic recession scenario would affect firm capital ratios

The stress capital buffer (SCB) requirement, implemented in 2020, replaced the quantitative CCAR evaluation and integrates stress-test-based capital requirements with non-stress regulatory capital requirements
Banks with $100 billion or more in assets are subject to the Board's supervisory stress test rule (12 C.F.R. pt. 238, subpart O; 12 C.F.R. pt. 252, subpart E)
The qualitative CCAR evaluation was incorporated into the standard confidential supervisory process in 2019
Large supervised banking organizations have more than doubled their aggregate common equity capital since 2009
The Federal Reserve conducts the stress test annually using at least two different scenarios to test bank capital adequacy
why_it_matters: This source explains the regulatory framework governing how the Federal Reserve ensures large banks maintain adequate capital buffers. The stress test and SCB framework directly affect bank capital requirements, dividend and buyback capacity, and systemic resilience. Market participants monitor these requirements as they influence bank behavior, lending capacity, and market liquidity during stress periods.
market_structure_context: The stress testing framework is a core component of bank supervision that affects market structure by ensuring large banks maintain sufficient capital to absorb losses during recessions. The SCB requirement integrates stress test results with regulatory capital, creating a forward-looking risk-sensitive framework that shapes how banks manage their balance sheets and capital distributions.
important_numbers: $100 billion in assets (threshold for stress test applicability)
2013 (Dodd-Frank Act Stress Test and CCAR initiation)
